claims.statement: SDP is made URL-safe for link transport via sdp-compact compaction plus character substitutions (/ -> _, + -> ~, = -> -) on encode and their reversal on decode, with an isOffer flag matching the SDP role; sdpDecode throws synchronously on malformed input (empty string, invalid base64, or a decompressed payload that is not SDP), so callers of user-controllable input must guard with try/catch (documented in source at PR #45; tests/sdp-robustness.test.mjs pins the throw behavior).

The offer link is built with buildURL(appBaseFrom(location.href), 'receive', ...) — the base is the app's deployment base: the URL's origin plus the pathname up to and including its last '/' (the containing directory of the offer page, which is always the deployment's base-root page), dropping the query string, any fragment, and an incidental leaf component (e.g. index.html) in one step while preserving sub-path deployments (an org GitHub Pages site or self-hosted build under /<sub>/); the origin-only base from PR #120 regressed sub-path hosts by dropping that location, so PR #123 replaced it with appBaseFrom, which stays byte-identical to the origin-only output for domain-root deployments; the query params are s (encoded offer SDP, required), i (ICE server override — the shared-predicate-resolved value, omitted when equal to the default), c (chunk size, omitted when default), and p (base64 SPKI RSA public key from the once-per-offer-minted keypair, only when encryption is on); empty values are dropped by buildURL.

The user-controllable 'c' URL param is validated against CHUNK_SIZE_OPTIONS (8/16/32/64/128 KB, the same single source of truth the sender options UI offers); NaN, 0, negative, or non-listed values all fall back to the 32 KB default chunk size.

The answer-code wire format is sdpEncode(localAnswerSdp) + '|' + publicKeyBase64 (key empty when the receiver downgraded to plaintext — a valid, intentional artifact); the offer peer's acceptAnswer first refuses to signal a dead peer (PR #104): if the channel's death handler already ran (or a racing regeneration closed the peer), it checks !connection || connection.connectionState === 'closed' and toasts 'Connection lost — generate a new offer to connect' instead of reaching setRemoteDescription on a closed peer, which would only fail with a misleading 'Invalid answer code'; it then parses the code with parseAnswerCode, which splits on the LAST '|' and distinguishes a missing separator from a well-formed empty-key code (which follows the receiver into plaintext via effectiveEncrypt=false instead of dead-ending the handshake), and on a missing separator or damaged non-empty key toasts 'Invalid encryption key in answer code' and aborts before setRemoteDescription; a key present in the code pins the session to encrypted; the SDP decode + setRemoteDescription runs inside its own try/catch that toasts 'Invalid answer code' on malformed SDP (PR #45); the receive page likewise decodes the user-controllable s param and calls setRemoteDescription inside a try/catch that toasts 'Invalid SDP in link' instead of crashing the page during load (PR #45).

Both sides wait for ICE candidates to drain before freezing the SDP into the shareable artifact, but a 3-second WAIT_ICE_CANDIDATES_TIMEOUT builds the link/answer code from the current localDescription anyway so the connection forms rather than hanging; on the offer side the RSA keypair is minted once at the top of generateOfferLink and a per-invocation offerBuilt flag claims the build synchronously so the two paths build the link at most once, and the whole generation is try/catch-guarded so a construction/offer failure toasts 'Could not generate the offer' instead of leaving the spinner stuck. Regeneration is generation-safe: before minting, the pending ICE-candidate timer is cleared, the old data channel's handlers are nulled and it is closed, the old RTCPeerConnection is closed (guarded on connectionState !== 'closed' since close() throws InvalidStateError on an already-settled peer), the settled peer crypto is reset (rsaPub = undefined, effectiveEncrypt re-pinned from the live setting, so the new generation never encrypts with the previous peer's RSA key — PR #68) and the dead generation's UI state (new-file badge, isConnecting, pending answer code, and the dead generation's offerLink) is cleared, and a monotonically increasing offerGeneration counter is bumped; the timeout fallback re-checks its captured generation at fire time so a stale timer holding the previous generation's public key can never build a link with the old key. A failed generation is also torn down with the same guarded shape (PR #108): the offer-creation catch clears the just-started ICE-candidate timer, nulls the four handlers on the just-created data channel before dataChannel.close() and resets it to undefined, and closes the just-created RTCPeerConnection guarded on connectionState !== 'closed' — otherwise the failed peer's ICE agent/UDP sockets/STUN keepalives would leak and late-firing channel handlers could stomp the current generation's UI. Since PR #135 the offer page therefore carries exactly two local guarded connection.close() sites (the regeneration teardown and the offer-creation catch) — the two channel-death handlers no longer close the peer locally, their guarded release living in the shared src/utils/channelTeardown.ts helper, which tests/dead-channel-peer-close.test.mjs asserts (no page carries a local guarded close inside a death handler; the offer page closes the peer in exactly those two local places; ReceivePage locally never does).

The offer peer creates the data channel (ordered:false) and the answer peer receives it via ondatachannel; both pin dataChannel.binaryType = 'arraybuffer' at channel acquisition (offer at the createDataChannel site, answer at ondatachannel) before the onopen wiring, because WebRTC's default 'blob' would make new Uint8Array(Blob) zero-length and Message.decode silently drop every frame (guaranteed no-op transfer, PR #95); both install the same handlePeerMessage handler from src/utils/peerMessage.ts (deduplicated from two identical per-page handlers, PR #71) with Message.decode on peer-controlled bytes guarded by try/catch (toast + drop the frame instead of an uncaught crash, PR #46) and unlock the Send/Receive transfer UI on channel open. Both pages additionally wire the channel's onerror/onclose to the shared createChannelTeardown() helper's handlers (src/utils/channelTeardown.ts, PR #135 — deduplicated from the two copy-pasted per-page death blocks, mirroring the channelSender.ts guarded-send and peerMessage.ts handler dedups): the helper is the single place that toasts ('WebRTC error' on onerror, 'Disconnected' on onclose), resets the page's isConnecting, runs the page-specific lost hook (OfferPage's onChannelLost clears the dead generation's offerLink; ReceivePage passes none), propagates the connection-lost state into both file pipelines via sender?.onChannelClose()/receiver?.onChannelClose() (PR #74; the onChannelClose bodies and the guarded send() live in the shared src/utils/channelSender.ts helper, PR #97), and releases the RTCPeerConnection guarded on connectionState !== 'closed' (PR #104): closing the data channel alone does not close the RTCPeerConnection — its ICE agent, UDP sockets, and STUN/TURN keepalives would stay live for the rest of the page's lifetime; the guard prevents InvalidStateError from an error-then-close double-fire or a racing regeneration. The helper's getConnection option must read the CURRENT RTCPeerConnection at fire time, not a captured one: the offer page reassigns its connection to a new peer on every regeneration, so a handler that survives a regeneration race must close the peer that actually owns the dying generation (ReceivePage's connection is a const, so a plain getter covers it too). No page carries its own guarded connection.close() inside a death handler anymore. Pinned by tests/peer-message-handler.test.mjs (including a static guard asserting binaryType = 'arraybuffer' exactly once per page at the acquisition site), tests/channel-sender.test.mjs, tests/channel-teardown.test.mjs (the helper's contract: toast/state-reset/lost-hook/pipeline-propagation/guarded-close behavior, and the live-peer getter), and tests/dead-channel-peer-close.test.mjs (static guard: neither page's dataChannel.onclose or onerror handler carries a local guarded connection.close() — that close now lives in the helper; OfferPage.acceptAnswer bails before setRemoteDescription when the peer is missing or closed, and the offer page closes the peer in exactly two local places — the regeneration teardown + the PR #108 offer-creation catch — while ReceivePage locally never does).

ICE configuration is resolved through the shared isSupportedIceServer predicate (built-in STUN allowlist — including stuns: for the TLS-served nextcloud relay — plus any well-formed stun/stuns/turn/turns URL) on BOTH sides: the offer page resolves its RTCPeerConnection iceServers and the emitted 'i' link param through resolveIceServer, and the receive page accepts 'i' only when it passes the same predicate, falling back to the default with an error toast otherwise — so a custom/TURN server chosen on the sender is always honored by the receiver and no asymmetric ICE configuration can break NAT traversal or TURN relaying.

QR exchange replaces keyboard entry: QrModal renders the offer link or answer code as a QR (byte mode via `new QRByte(data)` with no custom callback — the library's built-in UTF-8 encoder, surrogate-pair aware, emits the matching ECI hint EncodingHint.UTF8 = 26; PR #128 replaced a bespoke byte/ECI callback that previously truncated non-ASCII code points to their low UTF-16 byte and declared a wrong ECI US-ASCII 27, error-correction level M, auto version) via buildQrDataUrl in src/utils/qr.ts with the data URL $derived from the qrData prop so re-generating the offer never shows a stale mount-time QR (PR #53), and ScanQrModal decodes a counterparty QR from the camera, feeding the decoded text back through the same accept/copy path as pasting; the scanner is stopped explicitly on the programmatic close/success path (stop() in the decode callback and in onDestroy) so the camera stream + decode worker are released, and both modals use per-instance DOM ids so multiple modals on one page never share toggles or video elements.

Failure handling: a missing or empty 's' param on the receive page bounces to the app's offer page via receiveBounceTarget(window.location.href) — the deployment base with the 'receive' route leaf stripped, taking the containing directory of the remainder so a sub-path deployment stays inside the app (a bare-origin bounce would drop the peer off the app entirely on a sub-path host, PR #123) and no query/fragment can leak into the target — and then throws; the offer page's onicecandidateerror toasts 'ICE Candidate error'; channel death is owned by the shared createChannelTeardown() helper (PR #135): its onerror/onclose toast the error, reset the page's isConnecting, and on the offer side run the onChannelLost hook that blanks the dead generation's offer link to prevent reuse of a stale link; the helper additionally propagates 'connection lost' into sender?.onChannelClose()/receiver?.onChannelClose() so in-flight/queued files on both sides exit with an accurate 'connection lost' error instead of dead-ending or re-firing false per-chunk errors (PR #74; the onChannelClose bodies and the guarded send() live in the shared src/utils/channelSender.ts helper, PR #97) and releases the RTCPeerConnection guarded on connectionState !== 'closed' (PR #104 — closing the data channel alone leaves the ICE agent, UDP sockets, and STUN/TURN keepalives live; the guard prevents InvalidStateError from an error-then-close double-fire or a racing regeneration); offer-generation failures (synchronous constructor throws or rejected createOffer/setLocalDescription) toast 'Could not generate the offer', re-enable the button, and — since PR #108 — tear down the just-created generation with the same guarded shape as the regeneration teardown (clear the pending ICE-candidate timer, null the four data-channel handlers before dataChannel.close(), and close the just-created RTCPeerConnection guarded on connectionState !== 'closed'), so a failed generation cannot leak its ICE agent/UDP sockets/STUN keepalives or let late-firing channel handlers stomp the current generation's UI (pinned by tests/offer-processing-failure.test.mjs); and on the receive side an unappliable offer sets offerFailed (the setRemoteDescription try/catch and the generateAnswerSDP catch both set it), which replaces the perpetual 'Generating Answer' spinner with an error state ('Could not connect: offer from the sender is invalid') instead of dead-ending the page (PR #49).

The Copy Link and Copy Answer buttons — the keyboard-free path of the link/code exchange — never dead-end the manual P2P handshake silently (PR #79): copyOfferLink and copyAnswerCode wrap navigator.clipboard.writeText in try/catch, so a rejection (SecurityError in a non-secure context, NotAllowedError on denied permission, DataError, or navigator.clipboard undefined in some webviews) toasts a 'Copy failed — select the … text and copy it manually' error instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection that would leave the user believing the link/answer code was copied when it was not.
